23.text: Distribution of Products of the Hunt. — The spoils of the hunt are

24.text: divided as follows. Small seals are taken by those who have killed them.

25.text: The Chukchee say that these seals do not form an important object of the

26.text: hunt, because they may be killed singly, even directly from the shore: there-
26.note: Draft keyed a semicolon; the print sets a colon here — R6.

27.text: fore they are not included in the common products. The master of the boat,

28.text: however, is given a seal or two, even when he has killed none himself.

29.text: The meat and the blubber of thong-seals and walrus are divided in equal

30.text: portions among all the members of the crew. The heads are taken by the

31.text: master, and the tusks of the walrus go with the head. In due time these

32.text: heads figure at the ceremonial of heads. Then the walrus-tusks are divided

33.text: among those families of the crew that consist of brothers and cousins of the

34.text: master. The other members of the crew receive only a part of the blubber

35.text: from “under the whiskers” of the walrus; i. e., from the fore-part of the muzzle.

36.text: In dividing the hides of the walrus, the master takes that of the first one

37.text: caught; the man at the prow takes the second; and the following hides are

38.text: taken by the paddlers, one after another. If the number of walrus killed is

39.text: too small, the distribution may be continued in order the next year. Often,

40.text: however, walrus-hides are split on shore, and the number of the shares is

41.text: thus doubled. With thong-seals, whose hides are used for thongs and boot-soles,

42.text: and also form one of the principal articles of value in trade or exchange
